paper.title: HKOI 2020/21 Heat Event — Senior Group FITB

source.note: Official solution: https://assets.hkoi.org/ref/2021hs_sol.pdf. C++ is used where printed alongside C; Pascal omitted. The printed answer sheet has 20 Section B points.

prompt.en: In a room escape game, some clues have dependencies on other clues. That means the player needs to find out some particular clues before some other particular clues could be possible for discovery. There are 7 clues A, B, C, D, E, F and G: A and C together unlock E and F; B unlocks D; D and E together unlock G. Which of the clues can possibly be the 6th clue the player finds in the room? Write down the letters represented by the clues and separate them with commas. (Example: W,X,Z)
Complete the following program such that it calculates the value of f(x) correctly for all 1 ≤ x ≤ 100. f(x) = 1·2·3 + 2·3·4 + ··· + x·(x+1)·(x+2).

Complete the following program, so that it outputs the number of integers between 1 and n (inclusive) divisible by 6 or 8, but not both. It is guaranteed that the input n is a positive integer less than or equal to 10⁹.

source.note: The semantic harness evaluates the printed if condition for individual i values, avoiding an impractical 10⁹-iteration browser loop.

prompt.en: Now, complete the following program, so that it also outputs the number of integers between 1 and n (inclusive) divisible by 6 or 8, but not both. It is guaranteed that the input n is a positive integer less than or equal to 10⁹.
Complete the following program such that its output is hkoi.
Consider the following functions. Write down the return value of f(25).

displayCode.cpp: int f(int x){if(x==0)return 0;else return f(x/2)^x;}int g(){int y,i;y=0;for(i=1;i<=64;i++)y=y+f(i);return y;}

prompt.en: Consider f(x) = (ax² + bx + c) mod 3, where each unknown coefficient a,b,c is 0, 1, or 2. Each query chooses an integer x and reveals f(x). Enter the minimum queries needed to determine the requested coefficient, or X if impossible. Determine a.

Consider f(x) = (ax² + bx + c) mod 3, where each unknown coefficient a,b,c is 0, 1, or 2. Each query chooses an integer x and reveals f(x). Enter the minimum queries needed to determine the requested coefficient, or X if impossible. Determine b.

Consider f(x) = (ax² + bx + c) mod 3, where each unknown coefficient a,b,c is 0, 1, or 2. Each query chooses an integer x and reveals f(x). Enter the minimum queries needed to determine the requested coefficient, or X if impossible. Determine c.
The input to the following program is 801 integers between 1 and 100 inclusive. Complete the following program so that it outputs the inputted numbers in ascending order.

Consider the following 16×16 grid. Black cells represent obstacles and the circle represents the robot. Whenever the robot arrives at a new position (including the initial position), information of the adjacent 8 cells will be given and stored in array s, where s[i] equals true if and only if that cell is an obstacle. Given array s, the robot can take four possible actions: UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT. Complete f(s) such that repeated calling moves UP until it reaches the boundary, then follows the boundary CLOCKWISE.

```text
################
#..########....#
#...###..##....#
#....##..##....#
#........#.....#
#........#..R..#
###....###.....#
###.....#......#
#####.......####
#####.......####
####.......#####
##.........#####
#.....#....#####
#.....###..#####
##...###########
################
```

Adjacent indices: 0 1 2 / 7 R 3 / 6 5 4.

source.note: The checked interpreter does not model enum declarations; grading source maps the four printed enum members to distinct integers and checks the conditional behavior. Cases cover local observations reached along the official robot route.

targets.source: int UP=0,DOWN=1,LEFT=2,RIGHT=3;int f(bool s[]){if({{M1}})return RIGHT;else if({{M2}})return DOWN;else if({{M3}})return LEFT;else return UP;}
